extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners (U.S. patent attorneys/agents/paralegals) preparing and filing U.S. patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural guidance for submitting Application Data Sheets (ADS), supplemental ADSs, oaths/declarations, and naming inventors in U.S. patent applications (pre- and post-AIA distinctions included). Covers what to include in ADSs, priorities among documents, and form/execution requirements for oaths/declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested classification/technology_center and drawing figure in ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of information related to a suggested classification and TC and a suggested drawing figure may be provided in the ADS, but the Office no longer utilizes the suggested classification/TC and may decide to print another figure on the front page of any patent application publication or patent issuing from the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the submission may be provided for both provisional and nonprovisional applications filed before September 16, 2012, the Office will continue to follow its present procedures for classifying and assigning new applications and is not bound to honor applicant's suggested classification or figure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant patent Latin name and variety denomination
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant patent applicants should state the Latin name and the variety denomination for the plant claimed (Pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.76(b)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Latin name and variety denomination are usually in the specification and will be included in any plant patent or plant patent application publication if included in an ADS or patent application. UPOV database compilation requires Latin name and variety denomination; including this information in an ADS makes compilation more efficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative/registration number information in ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: ADS may include representative information such as the registration number appointed with a power of attorney (preferably by reference to a customer number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing this information in the ADS does not constitute a power of attorney in the application (see pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.32); the Office does not expect the ADS to be executed by the party who may appoint a power of attorney.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic priority/continuity data in ADS constitutes specific reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Domestic priority information (application number, filing date, status including patent number if available, and relationship) provided in the ADS constitutes the specific reference required by 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, or 365(c) (pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.76(b)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the ADS is considered part of the application, including continuity data in the ADS satisfies the statutory 'specific reference' requirement and the front page continuity data will be taken from the ADS if not in the first sentence(s) of the specification. Pre‑AIA 1.76(b)(5) does not apply to provisional applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign priority claims via ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign priority information (application number, country, filing date of each foreign application for which priority is claimed) provided in the ADS constitutes the claim for priority required by 35 U.S.C. 119(b) and 37 CFR 1.55 (pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.76(b)(6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The patent statute does not require any particular form for such a claim; providing the information in the ADS suffices. Pre‑AIA 1.76(b)(6) does not apply to provisional applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee information in ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignee information included in the ADS should contain the name (person or juristic entity) and address of the assignee of the entire right, title, and interest in an application (pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.76(b)(7)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including assignee information in the ADS does not substitute for recording an assignment under 37 CFR part 3 to have legal effect. Providing assignee information in the ADS is considered a request to include such information on the patent application publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental ADS: timing and permissible uses
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental ADS may be supplied after initial filing and prior to payment of the issue fee to correct or update information in a previously submitted ADS or to correct an oath/declaration under pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.63 or 1.67.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any ADS submitted after the filing date is a supplemental ADS. A supplemental ADS cannot be used to correct inventorship (37 CFR 1.48), correspondence changes (pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.33(a)), or citizenship changes (pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.63 or 1.67). If no ADS was originally filed, an ADS submitted later must still be titled 'Supplemental Application Data Sheet.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental ADS form and content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental ADS must be titled 'Supplemental Application Data Sheet' (variations accepted) and must be a full replacement copy of the original ADS with each of the seven section headings listed in pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.76(b) and all appropriate data for each heading (pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.76(c)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental ADS must be submitted with all changes indicated (insertions underlined; deletions indicated by strike‑through or brackets) and must be signed as it is a paper/amendment filed in the application (see pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.33(b) and 37 CFR 11.18). A supplemental ADS containing only new or changed information (i.e., not a full replacement) is not acceptable and likely to confuse the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to show corrections to data appearing in an oath/declaration via supplemental ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: When a supplemental ADS is used to correct data that was shown in an oath or declaration (e.g., foreign priority or residence), the supplemental ADS should show the original incorrect information with strike‑through or brackets and the new information with underlining.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This presentation ensures the patent (front page) will reflect such change. Example: to delete a foreign priority claim present in the original oath/declaration, the supplemental ADS should show the foreign priority claim with strike‑through or brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority of ADS vs other documents when inconsistent information supplied
rubrics_metrics.description: If inconsistent information is supplied by both an ADS and other documents (e.g., oath/declaration, amendment, specification), the ADS will control (pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.76(d)), and the latest submitted information will govern (pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.76(d)(1)), except as provided in pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.76(d)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If another document has more accurate information than a concurrently supplied ADS, submit a supplemental ADS to conform the ADS to the correct information. The ADS also governs when inconsistent with information supplied at any time in PCT/PLT forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception: oath/declaration governs inventorship and citizenship inconsistencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.76(d)(3), the oath or declaration under pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.63 or 1.67 governs inconsistencies with the ADS in the naming of inventors and setting forth their citizenship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If different inventors are listed in the ADS and in the oath/declaration, the inventors named in the oath/declaration are considered the inventors named in the patent application. Corrections to inventorship set forth in the oath/declaration must be made by a request under 37 CFR 1.48. If the oath/declaration incorrectly sets citizenship, a supplemental oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.67 must be submitted; a supplemental ADS cannot be used to correct citizenship errors in the oath/declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office capture of ADS information even when statute/rule governs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will rely upon information supplied in the ADS over an oath or declaration to capture data (e.g., citizenship, inventorship) even where the type of information supplied is governed by statute or other rule (pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 115; pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.41(a)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the oath/declaration contains the correct information but the ADS does not, the ADS must be corrected by submission of a request for correction and a supplemental ADS. If the spelling of an inventor's name is incorrect, a request under 37 CFR 1.48(f) is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class/Subclass information in ADS is advisory, not binding
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of class/subclass information in the ADS assists identification of an appropriate Art Unit but does not require the Office to honor the applicant's identification/request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staffing/workload requirements or the art crossing multiple Art Units may dictate assignment to another Art Unit; the Office will avoid allowing forum shopping by being bound to applicant‑requested Art Unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant authority information when applicant is not an inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: When the applicant is not an inventor, the ADS should include the applicant's authority to apply for the patent on behalf of the inventor (e.g., 'Legal Representative', 'Party in Interest under 35 U.S.C. 118', 'Government Property Interest').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This authority information clarifies why a non‑inventor filed the application (e.g., deceased or incapacitated inventor, Administrator of NASA). Correspondence information may be indicated by reference to a Customer Number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of PLT/PCT forms in lieu of ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective December 18, 2013, 37 CFR 1.76 was amended to permit use of Patent Law Treaty Model International Forms or the PCT Request Form in lieu of an ADS where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 601.05(a), subsection IV for additional information about using PLT or PCT forms instead of an ADS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declarations acceptable in lieu of oaths (37 CFR 1.68 / 28 U.S.C. 1746)
rubrics_metrics.description: A written declaration may be used in lieu of an oath for documents required to be under oath, provided the declarant is warned about penalties for false statements and includes required truth/belief language (37 CFR 1.68).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 28 U.S.C. 1746 unsworn declaration is acceptable if it otherwise complies with legal requirements. Form wording is provided for declarations executed within and outside the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution, authenticity, and provisional acceptance of defective oaths/declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: A document required to be executed in a specified manner may be provisionally accepted by the Director despite defective execution if a properly executed document is submitted within prescribed time (35 U.S.C. 26).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photocopies or facsimiles of an originally executed oath/declaration are encouraged since applications are maintained electronically; retain originals. If authenticity is questioned, the Office may require submission of the original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath execution venue, seal, and who may administer oaths (37 CFR 1.66)
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath or affirmation may be made before any U.S. person authorized to administer oaths; an oath in a foreign country may be administered before U.S. diplomatic/consular officers or authorized foreign officers, attested by official seal or apostille; the oath is valid if it complies with laws of the state or country where made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An attorney in the application is not barred from administering the oath if permitted by local law (District of Columbia prohibits it). When the certifying officer lacks a seal, official character must be established by competent evidence (e.g., certificate from a clerk of a court). Some jurisdictions do not require a notary seal but require the official title on the oath.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue must correspond to notary jurisdiction on oath
rubrics_metrics.description: The venue portion of an oath indicating where the oath is taken must correspond to the county/state in the seal; if venue and seal do not correspond, the jurisdiction of the notary must be determined from the notary's statements on the oath.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If venue and notary jurisdiction do not correspond, the oath is improper; submit a new oath/declaration or a certificate of the notary that the oath was taken within his/her jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming inventors requirement (37 CFR 1.41 / MPEP § 602.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application must include, or be amended to include, the name of the inventor for any invention claimed in the application. Inventorship may be set forth in the ADS or the inventor's oath/declaration depending on filing timing and form (37 CFR 1.41).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For nonprovisional applications, the inventorship is the inventor(s) set forth in the ADS filed before or concurrently with the inventor's oath/declaration; otherwise it is the inventorship set forth in the oath/declaration. For provisional applications, inventorship is set forth in the cover sheet per 37 CFR 1.51(c)(1). Corrections of inventorship after filing must be pursuant to 37 CFR 1.48. If neither ADS nor oath/declaration is filed, provide inventor names when filing application papers or a unique alphanumeric identifier to aid matching of subsequent papers; unsigned ADS is treated as a transmittal letter.
